provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
The output is twice the input size in each dimension. Each input cell becomes a 2x2 block in the output. A cell that is not background (originally colour 5, now palette[5]) gets the checker motif. A background cell (palette[0]) gets a block filled with palette[0].

In the original orientation, the motif has palette[1] on the main diagonal and palette[2] on the anti-diagonal. The D4 transform maps blocks to blocks, so only the pattern inside each block changes. A row reversal swaps the two diagonals, and so does each clockwise quarter turn. The emitted program therefore swaps the two motif colours when exactly one of these holds: the transform includes a reflection (d4 >= 4), or it includes an odd number of quarter turns. The program works directly in visible coordinates and handles rectangular grids of any size.
draft_notes.limitations: No tests were run. The program assumes that every cell which is not background should become a motif, as in the generator, where the only non-background input colour is 5. The background colour is fixed to palette[0] rather than inferred from the demonstrations. The fixtures agree with this uniform rule.
